log.detail:
REVISION REQUEST
Working file with the current ad: /var/folders/t4/btnwp3jj6sq4tg_x2p3kyvgr0000gn/T/forma-edit-x8VW0O/creative.html
Original brief: {"scenario":"TOGGLE CONCEPTS · 8s · SILENT · "TEN MORE HOOKS"

IDEA
Performance wants ten more hooks by Friday. Brand wants every one of them to still look like the brand. Toggle Concepts gives both teams what they asked for.

SYSTEM
Colours: Gray #F1F1F1 page, Navy #0C2B3F, Sky #B4E4FA, White. Signal Orange #FF4F17 appears once per screen, as the experts' check badge.
Type: Inter Tight. Headlines 600, tracking −3.5%, leading 0.95, sentence case. Labels 500 in caps with +6% tracking. Button 700 in caps.
Logo: the supplied toggle-concepts-lockup SVG, navy on light and white on navy. It sits top-left in every scene, about 3% of the short side, inside the safe zone.
Shapes: tiles have a 32px radius, ad previews 14px, tags 8px (not clickable), and the CTA is a 999px pill.
Recurring element: one KITE ad card, taken from the real engine demo on concepts.toggle.studio. Use frames captured from the demo and don't write new KITE copy. Add a small "DEMO BRAND" tag on the card so KITE never reads as a client.
Motion: the brand rules come first. Expo.out / power4.out, no bounce, overshoot or squash. Text comes in with a masked line reveal (yPercent 105→0) plus a 0.2s blur-to-sharp. Wipes use cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1).
Safe areas: 108px margins. In 9:16, keep the top 250px and bottom 340px clear. In 16:9, keep the bottom 140px clear. No text under 28px.

HOOK · 0.0–2.4s
On screen: a gray #F1F1F1 page. A navy tile bleeds off the right edge (and the bottom in 9:16) and holds the KITE card. The card drifts slowly, scale 1→1.03 over 2.4s.
Frame 0 (the thumbnail) is already complete: the logo, the card and voice A are all set.
- Voice A, navy 600, with the micro-label "PERFORMANCE" above it:
  "Ten more hooks by Friday?"
- 0.70: a sky plate draws in from the left (scaleX 0→1, 0.45s, power3.out).
- 0.85: voice B reveals on the plate, line by line (0.6s, expo.out, 0.06s stagger), with the micro-label "BRAND":
  "Only if they look like us."
- Both lines stay readable from 1.45 to 2.2.
Transition (2.20–2.85): the copy masks out upward (0.3s, power2.in). The navy tile expands from the hero until it fills the frame (0.6s, expo.inOut). The card rides with it into its PROOF position.

PROOF · 2.4–5.0s
On screen: a full navy field with the KITE card as the hero, cropped large. Next to it is the real "HOOK" chip row from the demo: Get paid · Rival · Benefits · Offer · No catch. Chips are white outline pills.
- 2.70: the headline reveals in white, top-left under the logo:
  "New hook. Same look."
- 2.80: the chips slide in by 32px (0.05s stagger, power4.out).
- 3.00 / 3.45 / 3.90 / 4.35: a white selection pill slides from chip to chip (0.32s, power2.inOut). Each time it lands, only the card's headline changes, swapped with a 0.3s masked reveal using the demo's own captured frames. The photo, layout, colour and type stay locked. That visibly is the proof.
- 4.45: an orange check badge appears on the card's corner (scale 0.7→1, 0.3s, expo.out). A flat white tag reads "Experts check every file".
- Throughout, the card drifts by 12px. Something changes every 0.45s.
Transition (4.75–5.35): a sky panel wipes left to right (0.6s). The card stays on top, shrinks into its end-card spot and match-cuts there. Two sibling versions of the same hook, Feed 4:5 and Post 1:1 from the demo, slide out from behind it (32px, 0.06s stagger).

OFFER + CTA · 5.0–8.0s
On screen: a sky #B4E4FA field. The navy logo is top-left. The card group (Reels, Feed, Post) is bottom-right and bleeds off the edge. The orange check stays on the hero card only.
- 5.25: the headline reveals in navy, 2 lines, 0.07s stagger:
  "Ten more hooks."
  "Still you."
- 5.70: a white tag draws in from the left (0.4s), then its text appears:
  "20% OFF YOUR FIRST MONTH"
- 6.00: the navy CTA pill draw

output.reply:
I fixed the end card. The PROOF hook chips (Get paid · Rival · Benefits · Offer · No catch) were showing through the sky end card, on top of the offer tag, URL and CTA. Their stacking order let them sit above every later layer. The navy layer now keeps everything in it underneath, so the sky wipe covers the chips as intended.

I haven't rendered it to check. This is a one-line stacking fix that applies to all three formats, and the layout, copy and timing are unchanged.
